描述_ZN: The Loquat with Fruits" scroll, modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 111 cm in length and 53.2 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "Every time I know the season because of the good fruit, I remember Li Gong with deep friendship on that day. Beihong in the Spring of the Year Bhai." Inscribed with the long rectangular seal in white characters, "Wang Sun of the Eastern Sea".　　The year of Yihai is 1935, and Xu Beihong was 40 years old.　　The picture depicts a branch of a loquat tree. Under the warm breeze, the branches and leaves overlap, and the golden loquat appears to be overflowing with the fragrance of fruit, exuding the ripe beauty of the harvest season.　　The author uses a large, full-bodied brush and ink method to directly point the color and ink, not seeking to resemble the object, but only seeking the changes in the dryness and intensity of the brush and ink on the highly absorbent raw Xuan paper. The dripping ink shows the freshness and vivacity of the fruit and leaves full of juice. The whole picture reveals Xu Beihong's unique understanding of Chinese literati painting's brushwork and ink interest.　　The seal on the picture, "Wang Sun of the East Sea", is one of the most popular seals that Xu Beihong inspected on his Chinese paintings. Xu Beihong's hometown, Yixing, Jiangsu, was near the East China Sea. Xu Mao Gong, a great general of the early Tang Dynasty, was once made the Duke of East China Sea due to his great battle achievements. Xu Beihong inscribed this seal not only to express his pride as a descendant of the East China Sea Xu clan, but also to add a legendary color and a few ancient meanings to his paintings.
